description: Provenance of the contract copies bundled with this jar. Two kinds of entry, on purpose: 'files' are frozen copies of FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification RELEASE tags (governed by selection rules V1-V4), and 'drafts' are unreleased development contracts read only through the rule V7 opt-in lane. Each entry records the source repository, the commit, the exact path, the SHA-256 of the bytes and the retrieval date; the family convention is that a copied tree is pinned by commit and digest together. CapabilityTest and DraftProvenanceTest re-compute every digest on every build, so a copy that drifts from its own provenance fails the build instead of quietly becoming someone else's bytes.
releaseAndBytesAreSeparateAxes: A release tag says which registry row a file answers to; a digest says which bytes it is. They are recorded apart because they do not coincide: releases v0.4.1 and v0.4.2 changed no contract, so they repeat the v0.4.0 bytes, and v0.6.0's fhr.json is the unchanged v0.5.0 bytes (FHR 2.1 did not move). The 'releases' map in schemas/bundled.json therefore points several releases at one frozen copy, and each copy is named once here.

identicalBytesAcrossTags.v0.4.1/v0.4.2 fhr|fhp|fhgff3: v0.4.0 same files (verified with cmp on 2026-11-14)

suitePinAnnotation.note: Advisory measurements, recorded beside the pin but never a substitute for it: the suite is pinned by digest first and count second. A count-only assertion cannot see drift that does not move the count.
suitePinAnnotation.delta: FIRST PASS IN WHICH THE CONTRACT BYTES MOVED, not only the suite: fht.json 29 430 -> 34 396 B (59ad9641 -> 4156353a, last touched by 86438f21, the FHT draft PR #54 pass: raw-main-only schema URL, regex-dialect-portable patterns, git-verified HTML binding pin) beside suite 72 -> 82 vectors (0 removed; 28 -> 30 valid, 44 -> 52 invalid; rule census C1 24 -> 31, C2 3 -> 4, C3 10 -> 10; 75 of the 77 recorded vector files byte-identical - only manifest.json and README.md moved). The two pins are not interchangeable - measured on this jar's evaluator, the suite's fht-fasta-molecule-type-mixed (expected valid) is REJECTED by the previous contract bytes because the MoleculeType enum grew 4 -> 5 with 'mixed', while fht-fasta-blank-version-separator (expected invalid) is ACCEPTED by them and rejected only by this one - so contract, manifest and the frozen copy in this jar move atomically; a suite-only re-pin ships a red or a lying draft job. Four of the 82 vectors remain the suite's own promotion=candidate-unreviewed cases; they are executed as the suite states them and are not presented as reviewed.
suitePinAnnotation.resolution: 86438f21c3a17a58334c97aed4955be1a2393522 is the last commit that touched BOTH fht.json and conformance/manifest.json, measured 2026-11-18 in a fresh full clone (FHT-Specification origin/main head 0311ddacbf7559d4160054d23db6fd06898f45a9; 86438f21 is its ancestor). Digests were taken with shasum -a 256 over full downloads and cross-checked against the contents-API blobs (git hash-object identity); every pinned digest reproduces byte-identically at 86438f21 via git show. Under the round-13 convention unified across the four native libraries, the commit recorded for a pinned file is that file's last-touch commit - never a floating default-branch head; the advisory freshness job compares digests against live main and does not depend on the label. The superseded annotation of 2026-11-15 (previous 66-vector era at 24d3b033, asRecorded 72 at be9bcc82) is preserved in this file's git history rather than erased.

This re-pin is one PR of the round-13 coordinated pass across the four native libraries, whose targets are the identical byte digests recorded in section 1 of that pass's specification; byte identity across the libraries is re-measured per repository, never inferred from another's prose. The contract bytes live in this jar; the vectors come from the suite revision above, and DraftHarness re-digests both against these values before reading a vector.
FHT.meaning: Unreleased development contract, readable only through the rule V7 opt-in lane and warned on for every record read that way. Not a released contract: no schemaVersion row in the shared schemas/versions.json, no w3id alias, no release tag, no support claim. Publication moves it out of the lane (FHT is scheduled as specification v0.7.0).

transport.note: FHGM records are not a file header. They ride inside an FHGFF3 header under one R15 extension key, so the lane needs two pinned files - the record contract and the transport overlay - each with its own commit and digest, and the file itself is still routed by its own released FHGFF3 citation under V1-V3. A records row without all five transport fields (transportFile, transportSha256, transportCommit, modelsKey, carrierFileKey) is refused at registry load.

baseSchemas.note: Shape copied from the owning repository's own base registry (FHGM-Specification development/model/base-schemas.json, registryVersion 1, measured at suite commit 06176262 as sha256 8feb36c1957d151e22da9833b7a3421b339b5f18475d054ebe7e54cabcf72eac (6 165 B), superseding the 33f3fd541fe6ad611376a559279a0f95a5b7901418a6e1e44aebc78f9a47370f bytes measured at 57118c52 on 2026-11-15; the registry TEXT moved with FHGM#26's URL-keyed selection, the registered BASES did not: both releases carry the same digests and tag-resolved commits recorded below, re-verified 2026-11-18 by git show at 06176262): every base is keyed by the SHA-256 of the exact release bytes, resolves its tag to a commit (and names the annotated-tag object), and never records a floating branch for released material. DraftProvenanceTest checks each digest against this jar's frozen copy from 'files' and each commit against tagCommits above.
baseSchemas.selectionRule: A carrier names its base through its cited schema URL; the registry maps that URL to exactly one entry (w3id with and without trailing slash, raw tag URL under both repository names), schemaVersion plays no part in the selection and the cited release's own bytes then judge it. Rules V1-V3 route the file and the overlay's closed branches admit exactly that pairing. An uncited, unregistered or moving URL (raw main, a superseded release) is refused, not substituted.

suitePinAnnotation.note: Advisory measurements beside the pin; the suite is pinned by digest first and count second. This very suite is the proof: its manifest passed through 36 001 bytes at 5d15ccc1 with the vector count STILL 31 on the way to 51 114 bytes / 43 vectors - a count-only assertion would have reported that step as no drift at all (measured 2026-11-15 from git log over the manifest's own history). A second, subtler class is on record now: the 2026-11-18 FHGM#29 pass moved the RECORD CONTRACT too (bf1553ca -> b7075e58, 9 564 -> 11 522 B), and it widened what a layers.model `pass` MEANS (see the delta) - a field diff shows bytes, a vector count shows census, neither shows semantics.
suitePinAnnotation.delta: 43 -> 62 vectors (0 removed; 14 -> 17 valid, 29 -> 45 invalid; rule occurrences B1 2 -> 3, K1 12 -> 15, K2 12 -> 19, K3 5 -> 7, K4 8 -> 11, K5 7 -> 7, K6 14 -> 17; the 11 K4-citing vectors split 3 valid / 8 invalid; all 58 distinct files the manifest references exist at the pinned suite commit, checked with git cat-file -e on 2026-11-18) - AND, for the first FHGM pass, both contract artifacts moved beside it: record contract bf1553ca -> b7075e58 (9 564 -> 11 522 B) and transport overlay d1619cce -> 533b3120 (2 613 -> 3 191 B). SEMANTICS WARNING that no digest diff or vector count reveals: FHGM#29 widened what layers.model `pass` asserts - beyond schema validity it now additionally implies trimmed invisible-character-free text, RFC 3986 links whose scheme carries a real host, non-blank deposits, NFC-unique model identifiers and a root-level gene target; a pass under these bytes is NOT the same claim as a pass under the 2026-11-15 bytes. The abstention question this widens is still open upstream: FHGM#22 (does layers.model presuppose feature rows?) with #27 and #28, and FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#241, are unresolved, and JS#11 documents the failure shape (a zero-row feature layer reported as reject where the validator says absent-layer; an empty ID= making K4 an unfalsifiable pass). The pinned bytes encode a model-layer semantics PROPOSAL; inheriting them is not inheriting their resolution. Byte-level coupling measured on this jar: five new invalid vectors (record-evidence-uri-javascript-scheme, record-evidence-uri-user-info-without-host, record-methods-protocol-ftp-user-info-without-host, record-model-id-trailing-space, record-software-uri-empty-user-info-and-host) pass the previous contract and fail only this one, and two valid vectors (fhr-specification-alias-v0.6.0, v0.6.0-citation-stating-1.1) are rejected by the previous overlay (seven-carrier enum; v0.6.0 paired const 1.2) and admitted only by this one - record contract, overlay, manifest and the jar's frozen copies move atomically.

FHGM.meaning: Unreleased development contracts for gene-model records, readable only through the rule V7 opt-in lane and warned on per record. Not a released contract and not a file-bound header type: no schemaVersion, no w3id alias, no shared registry row, no support claim. Publication is scheduled separately (specification v0.8.0).
